intro_en: In this lesson you learn to describe people, towns and things. You use adjectives for this. Adjectives are describing words, like "big" or "quiet". Japanese has two kinds: い-adjectives and な-adjectives. We look at how to say "it is" and "it is not" with them. We also look at how they go before a noun. You learn to ask "How is it?", "What kind of?" and "Which one?". And you learn to join two ideas with "but".

g08-1.explanation_en: きれい, 静か, 便利, 有名 and にぎやか are な-adjectives. At the end of a sentence they work just like nouns. 静かです means "it is quiet". 静かじゃありません means "it is not quiet". It is the same pattern as 学生です / 学生じゃありません from Lesson 1. In Tamil it is like "ஊர் அமைதி" (the town is quiet) / "ஊர் அமைதியானது அல்ல" (the town is not quiet). Be careful. きれい ends in い, but it is still a な-adjective. So きれくないです ✗, きれいじゃありません ✓. The word order is the same as Tamil: topic は (what you talk about), then the adjective, then です.
g08-1.tamil_parallel_en: な-adjectives work like nouns, like a Tamil noun-style description with "அல்ல" ("is not"). "இந்த ஊர் அமைதியானது" ("this town is quiet") = この町は静かです. "அமைதியானது அல்ல" ("it is not quiet") = 静かじゃありません.
g08-1.formation_en: N は + な-adj (without な) + です / じゃありません
g08-1.pitfalls_en: きれい and 有名 end in い. So people often think they are い-adjectives and change them to きれくない. For な-adjectives, use only じゃありません.

g08-2.explanation_en: Some adjectives end in い, like 大きい, 高い and 美味しい. They already mean "is ..." by themselves. You add です only to be polite. 高いです means "it is expensive". To say "not": take off the last い and add くないです. 高い → 高くないです (it is not expensive). In Tamil, "பெரிய" (big) changes to "பெரிதாக இல்லை" (not big). In the same way, the adjective itself changes here. One exception: いい (good) becomes よくないです. Not いくない ✗. This is because the old form of いい is よい.
g08-2.tamil_parallel_en: In Tamil the adjective itself changes to say "not" ("பெரிய" "big" → "பெரிதாக இல்லை" "not big"). The い-adjective changes in the same way. "இந்தக் கைக்கடிகாரம் விலை அதிகம்" ("this watch is expensive") = この時計は高いです. "விலை அதிகம் இல்லை" ("not expensive") = 高くないです.
g08-2.formation_en: い-adj + です ／ い-adj (drop い) + くないです ／ いい → よくないです
g08-2.pitfalls_en: 高いじゃありません ✗. い-adjectives take くないです. いくないです ✗. It is よくないです. 暑い (hot weather) and 熱い (hot to touch, for things) are both read あつい. Tell them apart by the kanji.

g08-3.explanation_en: とても means "very". Use it only in positive sentences (not with "not"). とても高いです means "it is very expensive". あまり means "(not) very much". It always comes with a "not" form. あまり高くないです means "it is not very expensive". Tamil has the same rule. The word "அவ்வளவாக" (that much) only sounds natural with "இல்லை" (not). Like in Tamil, these words come right before the adjective.
g08-3.tamil_parallel_en: あまり works like Tamil "அவ்வளவாக". It only goes with "not". "மிகவும் சுவையானது" ("very tasty") = とても美味しいです. "அவ்வளவாகச் சுவை இல்லை" ("not very tasty") = あまり美味しくないです.
g08-3.formation_en: とても + adj です ／ あまり + adj negative (〜くないです / 〜じゃありません)
g08-3.pitfalls_en: あまり高いです ✗. あまり always goes with a "not" form. とても高くないです also sounds strange. For "not very", use あまり.

g08-4.explanation_en: どう means "how". Use it to ask what someone thinks, or how something was for them. 日本の食べ物はどうですか = "How is Japanese food?". Answer with an adjective: 美味しいです. In Tamil you ask "சாப்பாடு எப்படி?" (How is the food?). In the same way, どう comes at the end of the sentence, before です. You also use it to offer something. お茶はどうですか = "How about some tea? (Will you have some?)".
g08-4.tamil_parallel_en: どう is the Tamil "எப்படி" ("how"). It is also at the end. "ஜப்பானிய உணவு எப்படி?" ("How is Japanese food?") = 日本の食べ物はどうですか.
g08-4.formation_en: N + は + どうですか
g08-4.pitfalls_en: どう means "how". It asks about how something is, or what you think. どんな means "what kind of". It goes before a noun. どう人ですか ✗ → どんな人ですか.

g08-5.explanation_en: Like in Tamil, adjectives come before the noun. "பெரிய கடை" (big shop) = 大きい店. い-adjectives go in as they are: 大きい店, 新しいカメラ. な-adjectives need な: 静かな町, 有名な喫茶店. Tamil adds "-ஆன" to "அமைதி" (quiet) to make "அமைதியான ஊர்" (a quiet town). な is like that "-ஆன". どんな means "what kind of". It also goes before a noun. どんな町ですか = "What kind of town is it?" Answer: 静かな町です.
g08-5.tamil_parallel_en: な does the job of the Tamil "-ஆன" ending. It joins a describing word to a noun. "அமைதியான ஊர்" ("a quiet town") = 静かな町. "பெரிய கடை" ("a big shop") = 大きい店. "எப்படிப்பட்ட ஊர்?" ("what kind of town?") = どんな町ですか.
g08-5.formation_en: い-adj + N ／ な-adj + な + N ／ どんな + N
g08-5.pitfalls_en: 大きいな店 ✗. い-adjectives don’t take な. 静か町 ✗. な-adjectives must have な. At the end of a sentence (静かです), there is no な. You use な only before a noun.

g08-6.explanation_en: To join two opposite ideas, put が at the end of the first sentence. この店は安いですが、美味しくないです = "This shop is cheap, but it isn’t tasty". Tamil also puts the joining word at the end of the first part: "மலிவுதான், ஆனால்..." (it’s cheap, but...) or "மலிவு என்றாலும்..." (even though it’s cheap...). Before が, keep the です/ます form as it is. Then put a comma (、). This が is the joining word "but". The が in 好きです (Lesson 9) does a different job.
g08-6.tamil_parallel_en: が works like Tamil "ஆனால்" ("but") at the end of the first part. "மலிவுதான், ஆனால் சுவையில்லை" ("it’s cheap, but not tasty") = 安いですが、美味しくないです.
g08-6.pitfalls_en: The ideas on each side of が must be opposite. If both are good, like 安いですが、美味しいです, "but" doesn’t fit.

g08-7.explanation_en: In Lesson 2 you learned これ, それ and あれ. The question word for them is どれ = "which one?". Use it to ask about one thing out of three or more. あなたの傘はどれですか = "Which one is your umbrella?". Like in Tamil, the question word can come at the end, before です. どれ stands alone. It does not go before a noun. You will later learn to use どれ at the start, as in "Which one is big?". For now, learn the 〜はどれですか pattern.
g08-7.tamil_parallel_en: どれ is the Tamil "எது" ("which one"). It goes at the end, like in Tamil. "உங்கள் குடை எது?" ("Which is your umbrella?") = あなたの傘はどれですか.
g08-7.formation_en: N + は + どれですか → これ / それ / あれ です
g08-7.pitfalls_en: どれ傘ですか ✗. "Which" before a noun is どの (Lesson 9). Use どれ only on its own. For one out of two, use どちら (Lesson 12).

items.L08-q01: 有名 = ゆうめい (புகழ்பெற்ற, famous). Both ゆう and めい are long sounds. A common mistake is the short ゆめい (like 夢).
items.L08-q02: 便利 = べんり (வசதியான, convenient). Here 便 is べん. 便 can also be read びん (郵便 = ゆうびん). That is why people get confused.
items.L08-q03: 忙しい = いそがしい (பிஸியான, busy). It is が, with the two dots. The last い is part of the adjective, so don’t drop it.
items.L08-q04: たかい = 高い (விலை அதிகம்/உயரம், expensive/tall). 髙 is an old form, used only in names. The normal kanji is 高. 古い (ふるい) and 安い (やすい) are different words.
items.L08-q05: しろい = 白い (வெள்ளை, white). 百 (ひゃく) is 白 with a line on top. 自 (じ) is 白 with one extra line. 日 does not have the short stroke on top that 白 has.
items.L08-q06: Hot weather = 暑い (வெப்பம், hot). 熱い is for hot things (お茶). And Chennai in May is not 寒い!
items.L08-q07: Hot tea is a thing, so use 熱い (சூடு, hot). 暑い is only for weather. Both are read あつい, so people mix them up.
items.L08-q08: After が (ஆனால், but) comes the good point 美味しい. So the part before it must be a surprise next to it: 安い (மலிவு, cheap). "Cheap, but still tasty." 高いですが、美味しい may look fine. But if something is expensive, being tasty is no surprise. So "but" doesn’t fit.
items.L08-q09: After が (ஆனால், but) comes 静か (அமைதி, quiet). So before it you need the opposite: にぎやか (கலகலப்பு, lively). 有名, 便利 and きれい are not opposite to 静か, so "but" doesn’t fit.
items.L08-q10: "How is it?" = どうですか (எப்படி இருக்கிறது?). どんな is only used before a noun. どれ (which one) does not fit the answer.
items.L08-q11: This sentence has a "not" form (面白くない). So "not very" = あまり (அவ்வளவாக, not very). とても is used only without "not".
items.L08-q12: "Not expensive" is close to "cheap" (安い, மலிவு). 古い (பழைய, old) is the opposite of 新しい, not of 高い.
items.L08-q13: Not lively = quiet (静か, அமைதியானது). 有名, 便利 and きれい mean other things.
items.L08-q14: Not new = old (古い, பழையது). 小さい (சிறிய, small) is the opposite of 大きい.
items.L08-q15: A な-adjective before a noun needs な: 静かな町 ("அமைதியான ஊர்", a quiet town; the Tamil "-ஆன" = な). Using の, or leaving out な, is wrong.
items.L08-q16: The "not" form of いい is よくない (நல்லதில்லை, not good). It is an exception. A common mistake is いくない. いい is an い-adjective, so じゃありません is also wrong.
items.L08-q17: きれい is a な-adjective, even though it ends in い. So the "not" form is きれいじゃありません (அழகாக இல்லை, not pretty/clean). きれくない wrongly uses the い-adjective rule.
items.L08-q18: An い-adjective goes right before the noun: 新しいカメラ (புதிய கேமரா, new camera). Don’t add な. It goes straight in, like Tamil "புதிய கேமரா".
items.L08-q19: "It’s tasty, but expensive" has two opposite ideas. So use が (ஆனால், but). と is only for joining nouns.
items.L08-q20: "What kind of" before the noun 人 = どんな (எப்படிப்பட்ட, what kind of). どう does not go before a noun.
items.L08-q21: "Which one?" out of many umbrellas = どれ (எது, which). どこ asks about a place ("எங்கே?", where?). The answer is "that blue one", so it is どれ.
items.L08-q22: Order: とても (மிகவும், very), then 古い (பழைய, old), then 町 (நகரம், town), then です. "Very" comes before the adjective. The adjective comes before the noun. It is just like Tamil "மிகவும் பழைய நகரம்" (a very old town). ★ = 古い.
items.L08-q23: Order: 安いですが (மலிவு, ஆனால், it’s cheap, but), then あまり, then 美味しくないです. あまり comes right before the "not" adjective. ★ = あまり.
items.L08-q24: "அமைதியான ஊரின் புகழ்பெற்ற கபே" (a famous cafe in a quiet town): 静かな町の, then 有名な喫茶店です. ★ = 有名な. Each な-adjective comes before its own noun.
items.L08-q25: ［1］At the end of a sentence (before です), a な-adjective has no な. So the answer is 静か. ［2］あまり goes with a "not" form. 便利 is a な-adjective, so use じゃありません. ［3］とても goes without "not", so use 美味しいです. 美味しくない doesn’t fit with とても.
